crime: Some nights her mother sat on her bed and hummed until she fell asleep. Other nights, the quiet was how she found out no one was coming. So {WITCH_NAME} kept the radio on all night, and the quiet never told her which night it was.

In the prison, a girl practised one pool shot alone in the recreation room in the evenings, with the door ajar. She didn't come every night, but when she did, she let only {WITCH_NAME} sit on the windowsill and listen.
Just before 8:40 one evening, the girl chalked her cue for her last shot. "Tomorrow?" {WITCH_NAME} asked. "Maybe," the girl said. "Don't wait up for me."

The girl took the shot. As the balls rolled, {WITCH_NAME} set them looping: roll, knock, drop, and back to the start, over and over. Then she came up behind the girl, pressed the cue across her throat until she went still, and laid her down behind the table.

At 8:40 she joined the prisoners at the upper railing, and they never lost sight of her until lockup. From the moment she arrived, they could hear the girl's practice shot clacking on through the door still ajar, until it fell quiet at 9:40.
At the ten o'clock lockup, they found the girl behind the pool table, the last ball resting in its pocket.

In the trial court, one prisoner played back the video she had taken on her phone while they sang at the railing. Behind the singing came the same roll, knock and drop every six seconds, and never once a hand reaching in to fish the ball out.

{WITCH_NAME}'s loops kept running after she walked away, until she let them go. Then the prisoners understood: all evening they had been hearing a single shot, looped before she came out, and it had gone quiet at 9:40 because she let it go while standing right beside them.
fields.epitaph: "Maybe" was more than the quiet had ever promised her, and she would not wait one night to let the quiet answer.
fields.epithet: The Girl Who Keeps the Radio On
execution: On the execution stand, a giant pool table lifted itself high on its legs. She lay at the far end of the felt, racked like a ball.

The rack lifted away. Slowly, the table tilted toward one corner pocket, and she slid down the felt with nothing to catch hold of. She rolled into the corner pocket and dropped through. There was no net beneath it.
She lay still beneath the open pocket, the tilted table silent above her.

magic.name: Encore
magic.text: She can make anyone or anything she sees repeat its last few seconds, over and over.
